original_question: Can one rigorously derive a quasi-one-dimensional Gross-Pitaevskii or nonlinear Schrodinger equation on a graph-like structure such as a Y-junction from a many-body Bose-Einstein-condensate model, for example by starting from an N-body theory on the graph and taking the N to infinity limit with suitable scalings, while correctly determining the vertex boundary condition in the limit? The boundary-condition issue is already open even for the simplest graph with two edges, namely a line with a defect.
target_in_paper: Introduction, §1.1 (not a numbered conjecture/theorem): the final open-problem discussion on deriving an effective one-dimensional NLS/Gross-Pitaevskii equation on a graph-like structure from a more realistic Bose-Einstein-condensate model, and especially on determining the limiting vertex boundary condition. The nearest text is the pair of paragraphs beginning “Concerning the mathematical setting...” and “A second point of view is less phenomenological...”, culminating in the sentence about starting from an N-body theory on a Y-junction and the remark that the boundary-condition problem is open already for the two-edge graph (a line with a defect).
correct_elements: Your draft correctly captures the paper’s second, first-principles BEC viewpoint in §1.1: a quasi-one-dimensional Gross-Pitaevskii/NLS limit on a graph-like structure such as a Y-junction; the idea of starting directly from an N-body theory on the graph and taking a suitable scaling limit; and the fact that the main unresolved issue is the limiting vertex boundary condition, already open for the two-edge graph, i.e. the line with a defect.
missing_details: The paper first frames the problem geometrically as a limit from nonlinear dynamics on shrinking thin tubes/guides meeting at a junction, not only as an N-body mean-field limit on an abstract graph.
The refined question should explicitly ask which selfadjoint vertex boundary/matching condition is selected in the limit on the metric graph, since this is the main point emphasized by the paper.
The paper explicitly asks how the limiting vertex condition may depend on the shrinking process for the tubes, guides, and junction size; your draft does not mention this dependence.
The paper also explicitly flags possible dependence on the boundary conditions imposed on the thin-tube walls, for example Neumann versus Dirichlet; this is missing from the draft.

The paper does not specify a concrete many-body Hamiltonian, interaction scaling, or mode of convergence, so the question should not pretend that a particular N→∞ scheme is already fixed by the paper.

The relevant effective equation is the one-dimensional NLS/Gross-Pitaevskii equation on the limiting metric graph ‘as defined before’ in §1.1, i.e. edgewise one-dimensional dynamics coupled only through vertex conditions; that setup should be made explicit to be fully stand-alone.

The N-body-on-the-graph route is presented only as a simplifying possible approach (‘to simplify the analysis’), not as the paper’s sole or primary formulation of the open problem; the refined question should preserve that status.
The paper says the line-with-defect case is already open as part of the same boundary-condition problem; this should be stated as a benchmark subcase, not as a separate unrelated problem.
refined_question: Can one rigorously derive, for a graph-like quasi-one-dimensional structure such as a Y-junction, an effective one-dimensional nonlinear Schrödinger/Gross-Pitaevskii equation on the limiting metric graph from a more realistic Bose-Einstein-condensate model—either by passing to the limit from NLS posed on shrinking thin tubes/guides meeting at a junction, or, as a simplification suggested in the paper, by starting directly from a suitably scaled N-body Bose theory on the graph itself—and determine exactly which vertex boundary (matching) condition is selected in the limit, including its possible dependence on the shrinking procedure for the tubes/guides/junction and on the boundary conditions on the tube walls (for example Neumann versus Dirichlet)? In particular, can this boundary-condition problem be solved already for the benchmark two-edge case, i.e. a line with a defect?
justification: The draft is aimed at the open-problem discussion at the end of §1.1, not at the standing-wave or fast-soliton results later in the paper. Its phrases “quasi-one-dimensional Gross-Pitaevskii,” “Y-junction,” “start directly from an N-body theory on the graph,” “suitable scalings,” and “line with a defect” all mirror the wording of the second of those paragraphs. However, to stay fully faithful to the paper’s actual intent, the question must also reincorporate the immediately preceding paragraph, where the graph NLS is first motivated as a limit of nonlinear dynamics on shrinking thin guides and where the author explicitly asks how the limiting vertex boundary condition depends on the shrinking process and on Neumann versus Dirichlet conditions on the thin-tube boundary. Since the paper gives no formal conjecture, theorem, or specified scaling regime here, the sharpest faithful rewrite is an open research question that keeps those dependencies explicit and does not invent a particular many-body model beyond what the paper states.
